review: Strictly speaking I came to this site expecting nothing, having spent eleven years in a megachurch whose worship was engineered to produce a response and having left over precisely that. This album does not do it. "Nachamu, Nachamu, Ami" sets Isaiah 40 and lets the wilderness stand for its full length before any comfort arrives, which is what the text does and what almost no contemporary setting has the patience for. I play it while my daughter naps. What I would ask for, properly speaking, is the lyrics published as text — I read before I play, and at present I am transcribing by ear, which is absurd for a site with this much care in it.
